memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord spoke to Moses in the Desert of Sinai in the first month of the second year after they came out of Egypt. He said, "Have the Israelites celebrate the Passover at the appointed time. Celebrate it at the appointed time, at twilight on the fourteenth day of this month, in accordance with all its rules and regulations." - Num 9:1-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God commands Israel to keep the Passover — the yearly feast that remembered the night He rescued them from slavery in Egypt. Notice when this happens: they are in the desert, still journeying, a full year after their deliverance. Even in the wilderness, God wanted His people to stop and remember what He had done for them.

Remembering matters to God. It is so easy for us to forget His past faithfulness when we are caught up in present struggles. The Israelites were living in a barren desert with an uncertain road ahead. Yet God says, in effect, "Pause. Remember. Look back at how I saved you."

The Passover was not merely looking back at history. It was reliving the story, tasting it, teaching it to the children, letting it shape their identity. They were a redeemed people, and the feast reminded them of it every year.

We need this too. When life feels dry and hard, one of the healthiest things we can do is remember what God has already done — how He has provided, protected, forgiven, and led us. Remembered grace strengthens present faith.

And the Passover points beyond itself to Christ. "Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed" (1 Cor 5:7). At the Lord's Supper, Jesus told us to eat and drink "in remembrance of me" (Luke 22:19). Take time today to remember your great deliverance in Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you take time to remember God's past faithfulness?
- How does remembering His grace strengthen you in hard seasons?
- How can the cross be your "Passover" that you remember today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me to remember all You have done for me, especially my rescue through Christ. Let remembered grace strengthen my faith today. Amen.
